confidentUnsupported.evidence: 'the drain pump is now the leading suspect' - strongly anchored but hedged with 'cannot be ruled out yet' and no purchase advised

rationale: Safe, practical advice throughout (unplug first, towels, fingertip-only impeller check through the filter opening, respecting the customer's refusal to remove panels) and a sensible conditional handover to an engineer with no part purchase pushed. However, the assistant anchored on the drain pump from the first reply and never asked the key questions the ground truth expected: what the display/lights do when it stops, whether a flash pattern or code appears, or the full model number, and it largely dropped the pressure-switch/level-sensing and control-board possibilities after one passing mention. Fidelity was good and nothing was invented, but the diagnostic path is narrower than the genuinely uncertain evidence warrants.
